_comment: temper-orchestration's expected-failure manifest, the sibling of
wasm_expected_failures.json (temper-drc-rs), wasm_expected_failures_geometry.json,
wasm_expected_failures_thermal.json, wasm_expected_failures_router_core.json,
wasm_expected_failures_design_bundle.json, wasm_expected_failures_constraint_compiler.json,
wasm_expected_failures_quality_oracle.json, wasm_expected_failures_io_types.json and
wasm_expected_failures_pcl_ir.json. Same contract -- see wasm_expected_failures.json's
_comment for why divergences are LISTED and executed rather than deleted or cfg'd out.
It is a separate file rather than more entries in a shared one because run_wasm_tests.mjs
exits non-zero on an ORPHAN EXCLUSION: a manifest entry naming no registered test. Point
the runner at this one with `--expected-failures
tools/wasm/wasm_expected_failures_orchestration.json` when the module carries
temper-orchestration alone.
THIS FILE IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS A RESULT RATHER THAN AN OMISSION.
It started empty at registration time (#985) for a stronger reason than "no divergence
found": the one platform divergence development turned up was FIXED rather than
catalogued. `pipeline::tests::*` (all 10 of the crate's `PipelineRunner` unit tests) hit
it -- `PipelineRunner::run()` read `std::time::Instant::now()` unconditionally for
stage-timing instrumentation, which panics ('time not implemented on this platform') on
wasm32-unknown-unknown, the same class of bug `temper-geometry`'s `bottleneck_geometry`
deadline check documents and works around. Unlike that case, `PipelineRunner::run()`
cannot avoid the clock read by not being called -- it is plain generic Rust exercised
directly by this crate's own `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests, not gated behind `python` -- so
the fix landed in `pipeline.rs` itself (a `ClockPoint` type that is `std::time::Instant`
on every other target and a constant `0.0`ms reading on `wasm32`) rather than as a
catalogued expected failure here. Native behaviour (every other target) is unchanged;
this is a genuine wasm32 platform divergence closed at the source, in the same spirit as
the `#941`/`#946` clock-bug fixes this catalogue's sibling files reference.
It stayed empty through the tier's Worker deployment (2026-08-11): no NEW divergence
turned up between registration and the Worker actually going live. Measured with
`node tools/wasm/run_wasm_tests.mjs` against the actual
`--no-default-features --features orchestration-wasm-test-registry` build: 83 registered,
83 executed, 83 passed, 0 failed, 0 expected-fail, 0 other. An empty manifest is NOT a
weaker gate: with nothing excluded, every one of the 83 executable tests is load-bearing
and any regression on wasm32 turns the step red immediately.
--- Registered (91) != executable (83): two exclusion classes stack -----------
packages/temper-orchestration/src/wasm_test_registry.rs names 91 tests across 16 modules.
8 of those never reach a wasm32 test invocation at all, split across two DIFFERENT
classes -- neither produces an entry here, because a test that never runs (in the relevant
build) can neither pass nor fail, and an entry would be an orphan exclusion:
* `host_math::tests::host_libm_symbols_actually_resolve` carries its own
`#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` -- the same dlsym/no-dynamic-loader fact
temper-constraint-compiler (70/69), temper-constraints (30/29), temper-geometry,
temper-thermal and temper-quality-oracle already catalogue under this exact shape
(1 test).
* Seven individual `#[test]` entries -- `phased_component_assignment_validator_stage`'s
`is_hv_safety_true_for_hv_and_ac` / `is_hv_safety_false_for_none_and_unknown`,
`feasibility`'s `record_loss_first_call_is_improvement` /
`record_loss_improvement_threshold` / `record_loss_zero_best_raises_like_cpython`, and
`pipeline_state`'s `phase_member_names_map_exactly` /
`phase_eq_and_hash_are_value_consistent` -- carry their own
`#[cfg(feature = "python")]`, scattered inside otherwise-eligible modules (see
wasm_test_registry.rs's own header, "the gate here is mostly per-*item* rather than
per-*module*"). `--no-default-features` turns `python` off, so these are absent from
BOTH this wasm32 build AND the native comparison build IDENTICALLY -- the same
`python-gated` class every whole-module exclusion on this tier already uses (the
module docstring's `preflight_stage`/`convergence`/etc.), just applied at
test-function granularity instead of module granularity (7 tests).
--- Native comparison (R19), diffed by name not just counted --------------------
`cargo test --no-default-features --manifest-path
packages/temper-orchestration/Cargo.toml --lib` (see wasm_tier_topology.json's own header
for why this crate's native_test_args alone carries `--lib`) runs 84 tests, all passing:
the 83 wasm32 names above, PLUS `host_math::tests::host_libm_symbols_actually_resolve`
(native x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu is not wasm32, so its own cfg does not exclude it there).
The 7 python-gated tests are absent from this native run too (`--no-default-features`
applies identically), so they are neither native_only nor wasm32_only -- they simply do
not exist in this feature configuration on either side, and are out of scope for the R19
join by construction rather than by exclusion. Diffed name-for-name: the 83 wasm32 names
are an EXACT SUBSET of the 84 native names, all 83 pass on both sides, 0 wasm32_only,
0 disagreement.
